reading.body:
Oracle reported $67.4 billion in revenue for the fiscal year ending May 2026, making it one of the largest enterprise software companies in the data, with AI embedded across its core ERP, HCM, and SCM product lines rather than offered as a standalone service.

The pattern here is integration rather than adjacency. Oracle's AI capability sits inside the autonomous database and Fusion suite, which means AI inference runs on infrastructure Oracle already operates for tens of thousands of enterprise customers. That model concentrates compute demand within Oracle's own data centers, and Oracle has made large public commitments to data center expansion to support it, though the data here does not quantify those facilities or their power draw.

The three MCP entries point in a different direction: agent-to-agent protocols, payment telemetry, and signed verification attestations for autonomous decisions. These are plumbing for agentic AI workflows, not end-user applications. Whether Oracle's revenue base reflects meaningful adoption of those capabilities is not answerable from this data. The 73 Texas regulatory exposures are noted but the data does not describe their nature or materiality, so no inference about legal risk is warranted.
